data.narrative:
Dusty Robotics is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Tessa Lau and Philipp Herget that has raised $70M+. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 1 public company and 8 private peers in Robotics & Manufacturing, including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Bedrock Robotics.

A peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow robotics cohort; only 1 same-stage peer exists in the dataset, below the 3-point threshold required for reliable triangulation. Consequently, the analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression to a $4M baseline derived from total raised. This method implies a valuation of $9M.

The triangulated range supports $7M to $10M, with a median of $9M. This analysis carries material uncertainty given reliance on a single methodology and sparse comparable data at the Seed stage within the sector. A more robust valuation would require either additional same-stage robotics peers or validation through cost-to-duplicate or revenue-multiple approaches, neither of which the current dataset supports. The $70M+ capital raised to date suggests substantial investor conviction, but without revenue or unit economics data, this cannot be incorporated into the quantitative framework.
